title: Google and Kaggle Launch Free AI Agents Vibe Coding Course — Registration Now Open | The Agent Report
highlights:
Google and Kaggle have opened registration for the second edition of their free AI Agents Intensive course, running June 15–19, 2026. The updated curriculum introduces vibe coding — building AI agents using natural language as the primary programming interface — alongside new content on production deployment and a hands-on capstone project.
The first edition in November 2025 drew over 1.5 million learners, making it one of the most popular AI courses ever offered. This year’s version adds updated content, new speakers, and deeper coverage of agent quality, security, and deployment.
Each day includes whitepapers, companion podcasts, hands-on code labs, and a daily livestream on Kaggle’s YouTube channel with course authors and Google engineers. Participants also get access to dedicated channels on Kaggle’s Discord for discussion and Q&A.

title: Agentic AI systems: from scruffy to neat | MIT CSAIL
highlights:
Agentic AI systems: from scruffy to neat
Google Deepmind
MIT CSAIL
11:00A - 12:00P
Contact lpk@csail.mit.edu for Zoom password
In this talk I will outline various ways to build LLM-powered agents which use increasing degrees of formal reasoning, ranging from maximally "scruffy" or informal language-based methods up to maximally "neat" symbolic / probabilistic model-based methods.
Level 1 is a simple reactive agent, Level 2 uses "chain of thought" (and optional tool use), Level 3 uses the LLM to learn a policy in the form of code (AutoHarness), and Level 4 uses the LLM to learn an explicit world model and performs model-based planning and inference (Code World Models).

title: Voice for AI Agents and Applications - DeepLearning.AI
highlights:
Voice for AI Agents and Applications - DeepLearning.AI
Course Beginner 1h26m
This course covers three practical integration patterns that meet you where you are: voice embedded in an application, voice layered onto an existing agent without touching its logic, and voice as a tool your LLM can call when it decides a conversation is the right modality.

title: RAG and Context Engineering program | MIT xPRO
highlights:
RAG and Context Engineering program | MIT xPRO
An eight-week learning journey that equips technical professionals to design, evaluate, and deploy retrieval-aware large language model (LLM) systems that perform reliably in real-world environments.
Covers advanced retrieval, context engineering, RAG architectures, evaluation, cost, security, and agentic workflows.
